llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (generate full TED-style talks) is reasonable, but the instructions ask the agent to collect concrete files, metrics, and decisions while the declared requirements only list an output path — that mismatch could cause the agent to read or include sensitive workspace data without that access being declared.

dimensions.detail: The skill claims to be a standalone creative tool that writes results to output/ted-talks/, which is fine for its purpose. However the runtime instructions repeatedly instruct the agent to 'collect concrete examples (files, metrics, decisions)' and to include actual filenames and metrics in the talk. The registry metadata only declares a workspace output path (write), not read access to project files or other workspace locations. This is a capability/requirements mismatch: producing the promised output legitimately requires read access to project artifacts, but that access is not declared.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md tells the agent to 'Read full conversation context' and to gather 'specific files, real decisions, actual metrics'. Those instructions give the agent broad discretion to surface and include potentially sensitive project data. The skill does not constrain which files to read or how to redact sensitive values; it also instructs inclusion of exact filenames and numeric metrics, which increases risk of accidental exposure.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install steps, no code files, and no external downloads. This is the lowest install risk — nothing will be written to disk beyond the normal agent output.

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials (appropriate for a creative skill). But the runtime instructions imply reading data from the user's workspace and conversation history (files, metrics, decisions) that are not declared in requires.workspace. Asking for access to concrete internal artifacts without declaring such access is disproportionate and should be made explicit.

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-on, is user-invocable, and allows model invocation (normal). It does not request persistent or cross-skill configuration changes and does not declare elevated privileges.

llm.guidance: This skill appears coherent for turning deep technical conversations into long-form talks, but it asks the agent to include exact filenames, decisions, and numeric metrics — which can reveal sensitive internal data. Before installing or running it: 1) Confirm what workspace read permissions the agent will have; prefer limiting it to a safe, non-sensitive test project. 2) If you want to keep secrets private, instruct the agent (or modify the skill) to redact or anonymize filenames/metrics. 3) Ask the maintainer to update the skill metadata to explicitly declare read access (which folders) or to provide an option that avoids including concrete file/metric details. 4) Test the skill on dummy data first. If you cannot verify or restrict workspace reads, treat outputs as potentially sensitive.
